2026 Compensation Positioning
$100K–$130K Illustrative target base / year
ROLE-DEPENDENT · NOT A BADGE PREMIUM

Market context and compensation caveat: The $100,000–$130,000 figure is an illustrative target range for relevant experienced Linux / cloud infrastructure roles, not a salary survey result or a guaranteed increase attributable to training. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reports a May 2025 median of $99,130 for network and computer systems administrators, with the highest 10% earning above $155,050 (BLS wage data). Foote Partners tracks cash premiums for specific IT skills and certifications, but its market averages cannot be applied directly to these badges or stacked 71 times (Foote Partners methodology and market trends). Skillsoft’s 2025 report describes employer-perceived business value from certified staff; it does not establish a personal salary premium for course badges (Skillsoft 2025 report). The 71+ items strengthen evidence of structured learning and practical exposure, especially when paired with demonstrable production experience, projects, and current technical interviews; they do not independently prove 71 professional certifications or a fixed annual pay increase. Relevant target titles: Senior Linux Systems Administrator, Linux Infrastructure Engineer, Cloud Support Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), and Platform Engineer. For roles requiring deep production engineering, automation, Kubernetes, Terraform, or current cloud architecture experience, target compensation should be calibrated to the actual job description and location.
